summary: Peter Koret works in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kornicki, an expert in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Oxford and under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida. He held posts at the University of Tasmania, Kyoto University, Robinson College, and the University of Cambridge.

A scholar in linguistics, Peter Kuhlmann studied under doctoral supervisor Rosemarie Lühr from circa 1990 to 1993. He later held academic posts at the University of Giessen (1994–2002), University of Düsseldorf (2002–2004), and University of Göttingen (circa 2004).

Peter M. Scharf specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, Ludo Rocher, Shrinarayan Mishra, and Narendranath Pandey, and held a post at Brown University's classics department attested in 2000.
Peter Masefield is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under L. P. N. Perera and doctoral supervisor Ninian Smart. He also taught Nicolas Revire.

Peter Moran is a religious studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Tufts University and the University of Washington, where Charles Keyes supervised his PhD. His teachers included Ngawang Nornang, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche.

Peter N. Gregory specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Kuroda Institute, Komazawa University, and Smith College.

Indologist Peter Peterson studied under Theodor Aufrecht at the University of Edinburgh and later at Balliol College, Oxford. From circa 1873 to 1899, he was Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College and Fellow and Registrar at the University of Mumbai.

Peter Schreiner is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate under Paul Hacker at the University of Münster. He held posts at the University of Tübingen, SOAS University of London, and the University of Zurich.
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Washington, completing his MA in 1994 under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, studying under Dieter Schuh. He worked at the Göttingen Academy, held a visiting professorship in Berlin, and was appointed to Bonn's Tibetology chair in 2001.

Peter Skilling is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the EPHE and studied under Heinz Bechert. He held posts at the EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation, and several visiting professorships.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Clare College, Cambridge, he held posts at Reading, the Ure Museum, and the Courtauld Institute before joining the University of Oxford and Wolfson College in 2011.

Peter Zieme specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Berlin, he worked at the GDR Academy of Sciences, the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Free University of Berlin.

Peter van der Veer specializes in religious studies, Indology, and Sinology, completing his doctorate at Utrecht University. His posts include professorships at Amsterdam, Utrecht, Pennsylvania, and Göttingen, and serving as Director at the Max Planck Institute (circa 2009–2021).

Peter von Bohlen studied at Halle, Bonn, Berlin, and Königsberg under Franz Bopp, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He completed his Habilitation at Königsberg, where he became an ordinary professor of oriental literature in 1828.

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tartu under Leo Meyer, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and earned his Promotion at Jena. He completed his Habilitation and served as professor (1886–1896) at the University of Giessen.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert from circa 1980 to 1991. She served as a research fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz, attested in 2013 and 2016.

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held affiliations with the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and the University of Munich.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the Dzongsar Institute and trained under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.
